articles.body: A federation of European textile associations called on Tuesday for an import fee of €10 on fashion imports, the latest effort to stem the flood of ultra-cheap competition mainly from China. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Dr Sheng Lu, Professor at the Department of Fashion and Apparel Studies at the University of Delaware, says that it remains to be seen just "to what extent such measures would push groups like Shein to change their business model", adding that fast-fashion retailers may have to start to contend with "consumer fatigue".
articles.headline: 'Subtle changes pointing to consumer fatigue' a challenge for fast-fashion retailers, expert says

articles.body: Germany on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted "hybrid attack" involving an explosive-laden drone at a strategic airport last month and announced diplomatic counter-measures. The European Union expressed "full solidarity" with Germany, NATO assured that it would defend its members and countries including Britain, Estonia and Poland offered strong backing. Germany will close Russia's consulate in the former capital Bonn later this month, and cancel the contract for the Russian House, a cultural centre in Berlin, said Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.
articles.headline: Germany blames Russia for airport drone incident, hits back with sanctions

articles.body: Oil prices rose, stocks fell and bond yields spiked after the US launched fresh attacks on Iranian targets. Japan's 10-year bond yield hit 3 percent for the first time since 1996. The deepening global selloff comes amid fears over rising inflation and concern over mounting government debt, which in the US has risen above $40 trillion. Meanwhile, in the single-currency eurozone, inflation rose to the highest level in three years in August, driven by higher energy prices.

articles.body: Lake Ontario is now appearing as “Lake America” on Google Maps for US users, following Donald Trump’s executive order to rename the lake. Canadians still see “Lake Ontario”, while users elsewhere see both names. But the change is far from universal: Apple Maps and MapQuest continue to use Lake Ontario. MapQuest has remained defiant against the move and since surged to the top of the US App Store download charts.
articles.headline: Google Maps changes Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’ as MapQuest downloads surge

articles.body: Every day, new bodies are recovered in Nepal, but many remain unidentifiable. Several days after the disaster, some are already in an advanced state of decomposition. Morgues in the country's main cities are reaching capacity. Faced with the influx of remains, authorities have begun burying them without formal identification. France 24's special correspondents traveled to Bharatpur, in southern Nepal, to one of these burial sites.
articles.headline: Mass burials held in Nepal as bodies wash up after catastrophic flooding

articles.body: A lot happened during summer recess: France’s constitutional council struck down the core of a new law to ban social media for under-15s, but it did validate the extension to high schoolers of a phone ban already in effect for younger pupils. Why one but not the other? On this the first day of school across this country and others, we size up what's best for future citizens, parents and teachers, who are all grappling in this age of distraction with the lure of screens.
articles.headline: School without screens: Will France's high school phone ban fly?

articles.body: President Donald Trump has a vision for next week’s GOP convention in Dallas: a televised spectacle putting Republican candidates in front of midterm voters and top party donors just two months before the Election Day — with Trump himself headlining the show. But a POLITICO survey of more than 70 GOP candidates and members revealed that most either do not plan to attend or are still weighing whether to go. Dozens more declined to share their plans. The 45 Republicans cited a variety of reasons for skipping the first midterm convention put on by a major party in more than four decades. Some cited prior obligations such as fundraisers or events in their districts that were planned before the convention was scheduled in June . Others had personal conflicts, like weddings and family events, and still others raised qualms about the five-figure-minimum fees that party officials want attending lawmakers to pony up. And some Republicans in tough races are steering clear of the gathering — which has come to be called “Trump-a-palooza” in some GOP circles — as they face growing hesitation about associating themselves with the polarizing president so close to the election. “I just felt I'd be more useful in my district,” said Rep. Tom Barrett, who is facing a tough campaign to keep his central Michigan seat. “I travel a lot for this job and if I can be back home and see my family and do the job back home as well, then that's sort of what I lean toward doing.” Asked if the president’s remarks might cause him problems back home, Barrett said: “I can't control what the president's going to say at the convention, but I can control where I'm at, what I'm doing.” Several other Republicans in key races targeted by Democrats said they weren’t committing to attend. “I’m going to be in my district,” Rep. Zach Nunn (R-Iowa) said when asked about his plans, while Rep. Rob Bresnahan (R-Pa.) said, “I’m not sure yet.” Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-Colo.) isn’t planning to go, according to people granted anonymity to describe his decision. And Rep. Nick LaLota (R-N.Y.) said he instead plans to visit colleges with his daughter. Trump will be the headline speaker of the two-day convention inside the American Airlines Center, with Vice President JD Vance also set to address Republicans. Most top House and Senate GOP leaders will be in attendance, including Speaker Mike Johnson and Senate Majority Leader John Thune. Some potential 2028 presidential contenders, including Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), will also be in attendance, as will some Senate Republicans from marquee battleground races. Former Rep. Mike Rogers, who is trying to flip retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters’ seat in Michigan, and Sen. Jon Husted, who is working to fend off a challenge from former Sen. Sherrod Brown in Ohio, will both attend, according to their campaigns. Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), who is expected to be the next Senate GOP campaign chair, is also planning to be there. Johnson said he has been “promoting this everywhere” as an important event for the party but also acknowledged it’s a crucial time for some of his members to spend time in their districts. “They've got to all make their own individual decision … but the people that do come are going to have a great time,” Johnson said in an interview, adding that he expects high attendance during the convention. He acknowledged in a news conference Tuesday, however, that some members will need to be in their districts because “it's critical time right before early voting begins nationwide.” With Trump front and center at the convention, some Republicans are privately fretting about slipping presidential approval ratings in their districts amid the ongoing conflict in Iran, a trade war with Canada and rising prices from both. Other moves by the administration, such as a deal tackling beef imports to address affordability, have angered other key GOP constituencies. One House Republican not attending the convention who was granted anonymity to speak candidly called the event “a waste of time” and said the planning has been “a mess.” “You shouldn't be having to rally your base at this point,” the member said. “You should be trying to convince independents. Independents are not attending nor watching the midterm convention.” RNC national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre said in a statement responding to those claims that “the outreach and enthusiasm to attend, participate, and speak at this historic midterm convention has been incredible.” “Republicans across the country are rallying behind President Trump’s America First agenda that’s brought lower drug prices, lower taxes, and a secure border, and this convention will provide the momentum needed to expand our majorities in November,” she added. But even some Republicans who might benefit from campaigning with Trump said the costs members are being asked to pay to attend were getting in the way. Another House Republican granted anonymity to speak candidly pointed to the $25,000 minimum attendee donation suggested by the National Republican Congressional Committee, which is distributing RNC-provided tickets to members. “I didn't want to go anyways. That made it easier,” the member said. According to an NRCC memo obtained by POLITICO , that donation gives a member the right to book one hotel room in the committee’s block as well as two tickets to a welcome reception and the convention itself. Higher tiers of giving up to $100,000 come with access to additional rooms, tickets and events. An NRCC spokesperson declined to comment. Rep. Tim Burchett (R-Tenn.) cited the price tag in explaining why he is still “not sure” whether he would attend. “It's $25,000, apparently — I just got a bill,” said Burchett. With the convention being seen inside the party as a key late fundraising opportunity, several GOP lawmakers who intend to be there, including some committee chairs, plan to give much more than $25,000, according to three people familiar with the planning for the event. But other powerful members are taking a pass, including two of the most senior members of the powerful House Energy and Commerce Committee. Ohio Rep. Bob Latta, who chairs the panel’s Energy subcommittee, said he had events back in his district, and Virginia Rep. Morgan Griffith, who chairs the Oversight subpanel, said he preferred to be home campaigning. “I should be safe,” Griffith said in an interview. “But no member of Congress from the 9th Congressional District of Virginia has left voluntarily since 1952.” House Appropriations Chair Tom Cole said he is not attending because he has a dove-hunting event back home in Oklahoma. Several northeastern members, including Reps. Chris Smith of New Jersey and Andrew Garbarino of New York, said they have commitments in their districts related to the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. Less surprising are the alternate plans being made by moderate Republicans who are facing tough elections in the fall and don’t necessarily benefit from being associated with the president. A campaign spokesperson for Sen. Susan Collins of Maine said she will not be in attendance, citing a “long standing practice of not going to conventions while she is in cycle.” “I’m not a party guy,” said Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-Pa.) said in an interview Tuesday, explaining why he won’t be in Texas next week. “I believe in ending the two-party system. Get back to our roots as a country.” Riley Rogerson, Kelsey Brugger, Katherine Tully-McManus and Calen Razor contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Republicans aren’t exactly flocking to Trump’s midterm convention

articles.body: LAS VEGAS — Vice President JD Vance tried to make inroads with Jewish Republicans. Not everyone is sold. Vance’s closed-door speech at the Republican Jewish Coalition’s annual leadership summit Monday night went a long way in alleviating top pro-Israel donors’ concerns about his support for the U.S.-Israeli relationship, and it cemented their view that Vance would be a preferable choice to whomever the Democratic Party nominee is in 2028. But some attendees still have questions for Vance — particularly around his relationship with conservative pundit Tucker Carlson, who has long drawn ire from the Republican Jewish leaders for his criticism of Israel and outraged many when he hosted the antisemite Nick Fuentes for a lengthy podcast interview last year. "He allayed a lot of concern, but he failed to address his relationship with Tucker Carlson, and that left a lot of people wondering why,” said Josh Katzen, a real estate developer and member of the RJC board, speaking in his personal capacity. Vance, the current front-runner for the Republican nomination in 2028, has long faced skepticism from Jewish Republicans who question his commitment to the U.S.-Israeli relationship and his response to antisemitism within the GOP. In his speech Monday, he took both issues head-on, and largely appeased the skeptical crowd with his answers, declaring that “Jew-hatred is corrosive to the soul” and saying Republicans need to articulate to young Americans why an alliance with Israel is in the best interest of the U.S. But his meandering response to a question about Carlson and other podcasters left some in attendance yearning for more. “A few names: Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly, Joe Rogan, Nick Fuentes. They have platformed antisemites,” former Sen. Norm Coleman (R-Minn.), the RJC’s board chair, asked Vance. “How do you draw the line, in terms of … the platforms that you appear on? “I recognize a lot of people in this room may disagree with things that Tucker Carlson or Megyn Kelly or Joe Rogan have said,” Vance said, before pivoting to discuss Rogan and Fuentes, saying those are “two very, very different categories of people” and suggesting people like Rogan should be reasoned with, even when there are disagreements. The answer was not sufficient to some, who wonder about his longtime relationship with Carlson. Vance was a regular on Carlson’s Fox News show and credited Carlson for helping carry him to victory in his 2022 U.S. Senate primary in Ohio. In 2024, Carlson pushed for Trump to pick Vance as his running mate. “JD Vance allying himself with an individual who has called for Trump's immediate removal from office will make it harder for many of us Jewish conservatives to consider his candidacy,” said Shabbos Kestenbaum, a pro-Israel campus activist who spoke at the Republican National Convention in 2024 and spoke at last year’s RJC conference. “We hope this issue is resolved quickly so we can focus on policy, not personality.” Eric Levine, a major GOP donor and member of the RJC board, said Vance could’ve had “an incredible Sister Souljah moment” if he took on Carlson. “In my view, on the issue of Jews and Israel, there is no difference between Hasan Piker, Zohran Mamdani, Abdul El-Sayed and the DSA writ large on the one hand and Tucker Carlson, Nick Fuentes, Marjorie Taylor Green and neo-Nazis on the other hand,” said Levine, speaking in his personal capacity. “That is why I wish the vice president had unambiguously separated himself and condemned Tucker by name.” Conservative radio host Sid Rosenberg also wasn’t satisfied. Just hours after urging RJC attendees in a speech onstage to “give Vance a chance,” he was critical of how Vance handled that opportunity. “He had a chance to hammer @TuckerCarlson and @megynkelly but instead spent all his time defending @joerogan over Nick Fuentes,” Rosenberg wrote on X . “Look, he’s still better than any Democrat candidate but I don’t think he wowed the STRONG Jews in the room tonight.” Carlson, in a text message, said, “An organization that promotes and defends genocide is continuing to insist that they’re the real victims? I can’t imagine who buys this nonsense anymore.” Human rights groups have accused Israel of genocide over its conduct in the war in Gaza, which the country's leaders vehemently deny. Vance’s office did not respond to a request for comment for this story. An individual close to Vance, granted anonymity to describe sentiment within the vice president’s orbit, said there was no illusion Vance would win over every person in attendance, “or that every single person would love every single answer.” “The goal was to lower the temperature, extend an olive branch, and make clear that the vice president is an ally, not an enemy,” the person said, arguing that goal was “achieved.” Sam Markstein, spokesperson for the RJC, emphasized that the organization is a coalition. “There will always be many opinions within the organization,” Markstein said. “In an hour when too many public figures are walking away from the Jewish community and the U.S.-Israel relationship, the Republican Jewish Coalition will always stand with the leaders who show up. Vice President JD Vance shows up — and received multiple standing ovations with thunderous applause.” Vance, who was elected to the Senate in 2022, faces a fundamental disadvantage among potential Republican 2028ers: He’s still a relative newcomer to the Republican political scene. Others, like Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), have developed relationships with pro-Israel Republicans in both the Jewish and evangelical Christian communities for years, going well back before their respective 2016 presidential runs. Rubio has pushed to revoke visas from individuals accused of promoting antisemitism or supporting terrorism. Cruz has publicly sparred with Carlson , criticizing him of antisemitism. A Cruz-aligned nonprofit recently launched to take on right-wing antisemitism. Vance’s speech was his first at an RJC leadership summit, though he attended in 2022. It was the first time since 2019 a sitting president or vice president attended the conference, which draws some of the country’s most influential Republican donors. Not being a favorite among RJC leaders wasn’t an impediment to Donald Trump’s political outsider 2016 presidential bid. During that campaign, he was accused of invoking antisemitic stereotypes during a speech to the RJC and in a social media post . But upon taking office, he formed a strong relationship with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, culminating in the Abraham Accords and moving the U.S. embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem. Speakers at the RJC’s two-day summit this week frequently referred to Trump as the most pro-Israel president in U.S. history. But Rubio and Cruz have been fixtures at past iterations of the RJC’s annual leadership summit, and they maintain strong ties with the group’s leadership. (None have announced whether they’ll seek the presidential nomination, though Rubio has stated he will not run if Vance does.) Many attendees said Rubio is still the favorite amongst the crowd. “Every time Marco Rubio's name is mentioned in this conference, there's a spontaneous round of applause,” said Katzen, the RJC board member. Indeed, when Rosenberg urged attendees to welcome Vance in a speech Monday, he mentioned the hypothetical, “If Marco Rubio was here tonight—” and was drowned out by applause. Should Rubio not run for the nomination against Vance, other observers think Cruz will have the inside lane among the RJC crowd. "Ted Cruz is loved here, and he deserves to be loved here,” said Levine, prior to Vance’s speech. “Look, if it's Cruz and Vance, I expect that this crowd would be 90 percent Cruz." Ari Fleischer, an RJC board member and a former White House press secretary, said Vance made inroads — but building a relationship with the pro-Israel community takes time. "It's fair to say hearts and minds are changing, but I think it's also fair to say that when you come before the Republican Jewish Coalition, it's like when you come to New Hampshire to campaign,” Fleischer said. “After the third or fourth time, we let you know how you're doing.”
articles.headline: JD Vance courts Jewish Republicans. Tucker Carlson still looms.

articles.body: Allies of Texas GOP Senate hopeful Ken Paxton are planning a $15 million ad campaign starting Tuesday, the first major ad buy on behalf of Paxton in his battleground matchup with Democrat James Talarico. Two new ads from Lone Star Liberty PAC, the pro-Paxton super PAC, will air across 18 markets across Texas over the ensuing two weeks. They mark Paxton’s first significant foray on to the airwaves, jolting a campaign that has been clouded by concerns over Talarico’s massive cash advantage and Paxton’s electability. One of the new ads will lean into Paxton’s record as attorney general, highlighting Texas’ recent agreement with Kellogg's to remove certain food dyes from cereals and the state’s billion-dollar settlements with Meta and Google over privacy and safety concerns. “When they come after Texans, he comes after them,” a voiceover says in the ad. The other new advertisement accuses Talarico of aiding China’s growth at the expense of Texas residents, pointing to the Democrat’s vote against restrictions on Chinese investments, and argues that a Chinese billionaire’s ownership of land near Laughlin Air Force Base presents national security concerns. “China’s got Talarico. Texas needs Ken Paxton,” the ad says. “[James Talarico] voted to sell Texas land to China, pushed a Texas Green New Deal that would gut our oil and gas jobs, and stood with criminals over cops as the most pro-criminal member of the Texas House,” Lone Star Liberty spokesperson Sam Cooper said. “That record is too extreme for Texas. Between now and Election Day, voters are going to hear it.” In a statement, Talarico's campaign refuted Paxton's claims and accused him of being weak on China. "Paxton is the only candidate in this race that has cozied up to the Chinese Communist Party, going on a lavish all expenses paid trip to China and meeting with CCP officials while he was supposed to be serving us," Talarico campaign spokesperson JT Ennis said in a statement. "James has voted to support Texans’ security, privacy, and first amendment protections from foreign government influence.” The multimillion-dollar campaign comes as Republicans look for ways to negate Talarico’s war chest. The latest Federal Election Commission filings from July show Talarico with $21.5 million in the bank, dwarfing Paxton’s $1.8 million in reserves. That advantage, along with Paxton’s drawn-out primary runoff that forced him to focus on beating Sen. John Cornyn, has allowed Talarico to dominate the general election messaging battle on television. He’s spent $39 million on TV since the March primary, according to data tracking firm AdImpact. On Saturday, Talarico launched his first negative ad against Paxton, spotlighting his impeachment and labeling him “the most corrupt politician in Texas.” Although Republicans have traditionally been favored in Texas statewide elections, Democrats are optimistic Talarico can defeat Paxton. A Texas Public Opinion Research poll released Thursday found Talarico leading Paxton — 48 percent to 42 percent. Concerns about a potential Paxton defeat have prompted some Republicans to implore President Donald Trump to invest some of the gargantuan MAGA Inc. war chest in the Texas race. MAGA Inc. has over $400 million in cash on hand, and Trump publicly pledged to support Paxton financially.
articles.headline: Paxton allies launch $15 million ad campaign

articles.body: Republicans and Democrats are fighting over working class voters. Americans don’t believe the rhetoric. Fifty-five percent of Americans think politicians are just trying to win votes when they say they will help the working class, according to new results from The POLITICO Poll. It’s a view held by majorities of people who voted for President Donald Trump, who voted for Kamala Harris and who self-identify as working class. Only one in four Americans who self-identify as working-class say politicians genuinely want to help them. That wariness comes as both parties increasingly see working class voters as key to their winning coalitions. But The POLITICO Poll results show both parties face serious challenges to doing so. Neither party does particularly well with Americans who identify as working class: 38 percent of them say Democrats best represent them, while 32 percent say Republicans. Americans, broadly, are almost identically split, with a 37 percent plurality saying Democrats best represent the interests of the working class, while 30 percent say Republicans. Democrats wrestling with how to win back voters who have drifted toward the GOP — as their coalition has grown increasingly dominated by college-educated Americans — are locked in an intraparty battle over which wing of the party, progressives or moderates, best speaks to these voters. “We've struggled with the working class for quite a while and it's been a combination of being out of touch with working class values on a lot of culture issues and being seen as either not helpful or not helpful enough on economic issues,” said Jim Kessler, executive vice president for policy at the centrist Democratic think tank Third Way. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), widely considered the leader of the progressive movement, told Playbook's Will Steakin that progressive Democrats “are speaking to the needs of working families.” “It is not just traditional Democrats or independents,” he said. “There are a lot of working-class Republicans who understand that there's something wrong when we are the only major nation on Earth not to guarantee health care to all people.” Republicans, meanwhile, are trying to hold onto the gains Trump made in 2024 with working class voters — including Black and Latino voters frustrated with the Biden-era economy — at a time when cost of living remains voters' top concern. “With the [Iran] war, with gas prices, with cost of food, the working class is not happy with the president, and many who are independents and even some Republicans have said that he's forgotten about them,” said former Ohio Republican Rep. Jim Renacci. Who is working class? Complicating both parties’ efforts to win over these voters is that Americans do not agree on what makes someone working class. Neither do lawmakers and party officials. When asked whether the term “working class” describes them, a 59 percent majority of Americans broadly say it does, while just 31 percent say it does not, according to the survey conducted by London-based polling firm Public First. But when forced to choose from a list of labels — including wealthy, middle class, lower middle class, working class and poor — just 16 percent of adults say they identify as “working class.” Americans are also divided over what characteristics define the working class. Some politicians, including progressive New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Andy Schor, the centrist Democratic mayor of Lansing, Michigan, have argued the definition of working class is expansive — encompassing anyone who needs to work to pay their bills. “If you're not making enough money that you don't have to work, then you're working class,” said Schor in an interview. “The American Dream is to be able to work hard and get ahead, and people are not getting ahead like they used to, and they'll look at the folks that they vote for and think, ‘Who can help me to get ahead?’” The POLITICO Poll illustrates the difficult path for the GOP to solidify its gains with working class Americans as economic concerns continue to be top of mind: More than a third of this group say they are not currently employed. A 35 percent plurality also say Trump, not former President Joe Biden, is fully responsible for the economy and many oppose the war in Iran, which most say has made things more expensive for them. Half of self-identified working class Americans say Trump has spent too much time focusing on international affairs instead of on domestic issues. “I think [Republican candidates] just got to tell the truth,” Renacci, the Ohio Republican, said. “You just have to start realizing that those middle class voters are struggling and they're just looking for somebody who's going to understand their issues and problems.” The race for 2026 November will offer a major test of whether each party’s working class pitch is working, carrying implications that extend into 2028. Candidates in both parties are racing to flex their working class bonafides this cycle, leaning on their biographies to signal ties to these voters. Trump pushed that playbook to extremes in 2024, when he briefly worked the fryer and drive-through window at McDonald’s as part of a campaign swing through Pennsylvania. Republicans have continued that approach, with candidates and administration officials emphasizing their blue-collar roots on the campaign trail. Vice President JD Vance recently returned to his hometown of Middletown, Ohio, where he spoke at the steel plant where his grandfather worked. In battleground Georgia, Rep. Mike Collins — the state’s GOP Senate nominee — often touts his background as a trucker. And GOP Sen. Susan Collins has broken with Trump on tariff policy, saying his trade fight with Canada hurts working families and small businesses in Maine, where she’s locked in a competitive battle for reelection. These efforts come against the backdrop of increasing concerns about the economy, fueled by the ongoing Iran war . Democrats, meanwhile, are divided over which flank of the party can best appeal to working class voters, a fissure that burst into public view during primary season, when a slate of progressives prevailed in high-profile contests. “The working class are giving Democrats another look and we better not blow it,” said Kessler of Third Way. “Donald Trump got reelected based on the notion he was going to fight for you, working class men and women, and his first year and a half has been anything but that.” Some Democrats have made their working class background central to their pitch: Sam Forstag, a union leader and former smokejumper, is running in an open district in western Montana that Trump won by double digits in 2024. Bob Brooks, a firefighter union chief, is challenging GOP Rep. Ryan Mackenzie in Pennsylvania. But some progressives are still running into limits: In Michigan, one of Democrats’ must-hold seats in November, the state’s divisive Senate primary illustrated that debate in real-time. Progressive Abdul El-Sayed, who won the Democratic nomination, performed best in the state’s wealthiest and most highly educated areas , while moderate Rep. Haley Stevens did better in places with lower average incomes and where fewer votes have college degrees. Jessie Blaeser contributed to this report.

articles.body: <p>El ministro de Interior de España, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, ha exigido en una carta en la madrugada de este miércoles al director general de la Policía, Francisco Pardo Piqueras, que, “de ser cierto”, ponga en su conocimiento desde cuándo disponía el cuerpo policial de información que apunta a que agentes marroquíes dirigieron la entrada masiva de personas a Ceuta con un objetivo distinto al migratorio. El titular de Interior da este paso después de que la unidad de inmigración de la Comisaría de Extranjería haya remitido un informe a la Audiencia Nacional comunicando que la entrada de unas 70.000 personas el pasado 30 y 31 de julio pudo estar <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-17/la-crisis-migratoria-de-ceuta-desvela-un-memorial-de-agravios-de-marruecos-hacia-espana.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-17/la-crisis-migratoria-de-ceuta-desvela-un-memorial-de-agravios-de-marruecos-hacia-espana.html">planificada para colapsar el acceso fronterizo</a>. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-02/marlaska-pide-al-director-de-la-policia-que-aclare-si-existe-un-informe-que-senala-a-marruecos-en-el-asalto-masivo-a-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Las derechas unen fuerzas en el arranque del curso político para movilizar la calle en una protesta que auguran “masiva” <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/ceuta-el-mes-que-rompio-una-ciudad.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/ceuta-el-mes-que-rompio-una-ciudad.html">por la crisis de Ceuta y con la que esperan elevar la presión sobre el Gobierno en la víspera de la comparecencia de Pedro Sánchez el jueves en el Congreso</a>. El PP, a través de la Federación Española de Municipios y Provincias (FEMP), que preside, ha convocado este miércoles concentraciones a las ocho de la tarde frente a todos los ayuntamientos del país coincidiendo con el Día de Ceuta, presentándolas como unas movilizaciones “apartidistas” para expresar apoyo a la ciudad autónoma. Mientras Vox, que se ha sumado a la convocatoria, llama a secundarlas “contra el Gobierno traidor”. Los líderes del PP y Vox, Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Santiago Abascal, exhibirán unidad coincidiendo en la concentración frente al Ayuntamiento de Madrid. El Gobierno, que pide que las protestas se desarrollen sin violencia, acusa por su parte al PP de “instrumentalizar” la FEMP y de presentar como neutrales unas protestas ideadas en realidad como una “utilización partidista” de la crisis ceutí. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-02/feijoo-y-abascal-unen-fuerzas-en-una-protesta-que-esperan-masiva-por-la-crisis-de-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Feijóo y Abascal unen fuerzas en una protesta que esperan masiva por la crisis de Ceuta

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/JDFRWO6FIFFQ3BP75FPV7FIXZ4.jpg?auth=5cacf060ed3193efb0d320873a121b3110655c07275141aa3192f2a4223d227f" width="1534" height="1025" alt="Tarek y Salma salen de Ceuta hacia Marruecos este lunes por la frontera del Tarajal."></img><p>Tarek y su hermana Salma llegan mirando al suelo y arrastrando los pies. Vinieron <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/ultima-hora-de-la-entrada-de-inmigrantes-a-ceuta-en-directo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/ultima-hora-de-la-entrada-de-inmigrantes-a-ceuta-en-directo.html">a Ceuta </a>sin nada y se van sin nada por la frontera. Ni una lágrima ni una mirada atrás cuando salen de Ceuta. Ambos describen el último mes como “el peor” de sus vidas. Sin embargo, ampliando la mirada, su aventura ha roto una ciudad, se enmarca en una crisis con <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/los-servicios-secretos-ven-probables-mas-acciones-encubiertas-sobre-ceuta-y-melilla.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/los-servicios-secretos-ven-probables-mas-acciones-encubiertas-sobre-ceuta-y-melilla.html">ramificaciones internacionales</a>, con Rusia, Israel e Italia en el punto de mira, y ha puesto al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez frente a su mayor emergencia migratoria. “No puedo más, me voy. Aún no sé para qué vine”, dice Tarek, de 20 años, <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/ceuta/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/ceuta/">antes de abandonar Ceuta </a>hacia Marruecos por un camino de tierra —el único habilitado para quienes entraron de forma ilegal y deciden regresar— a un costado del control de pasaportes. “Quiero volver al instituto”, añade su hermana Salma, de 17 años, que decidió unirse a la caravana para entrar en España sin saber muy bien por qué. Tarek y Salma han pasado un mes juntos protegiéndose mutuamente y emprenden este lunes su regreso a Oued Laou, a dos horas en coche de Ceuta y a cinco de Melilla por la costa.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-02/salir-de-ceuta-por-su-propio-pie-no-puedo-mas-me-voy-aun-no-se-para-que-vine.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/XIHLLQKFPNEUXAQTS3GL3IWSFE.jpg?auth=d62dd2eb7aacfa6859620d0ef881f55d5617791b31a0912dcc4c4467f73b50f9" width="4417" height="2817" alt="Karim Molahid sale de Ceuta hacia Marruecos este lunes por la frontera del Tarajal."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/XFGMNW5WNNG7XG772RJATCXSVI.jpeg?auth=1d287e03d1f83f008b6985bc1db85226a846839a774b41a7d47f8e90c135db3e" width="1051" height="1496" alt="Karim Molahid se despide de su amigo en la frontera antes de salir voluntariamente este lunes de Ceuta a Marruecos por Tarajal"></img>
articles.headline: Salir de Ceuta por su propio pie: “No puedo más, me voy. Aún no sé para qué vine”

articles.body: <p>Si algo positivo nos puede haber traído <a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-30/ceuta-lo-urgente-y-lo-importante.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-30/ceuta-lo-urgente-y-lo-importante.html">la crisis migratoria</a> desencadenada en Ceuta por la llegada descontrolada de personas a través de la frontera natural es permitir que la política española recupere cierto nivel. Después de meses estancada la legislatura en la bronca y en esa pelea infantil para deslegitimar al contrario, tras tantos meses de cinismo y cero razonamiento, Ceuta <a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-04/por-alegrias.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-04/por-alegrias.html">obliga a resolver, trabajar y entender.</a> No cabe duda de que <a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-26/tiempo-perdido-en-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-26/tiempo-perdido-en-ceuta.html">la pasividad y la flojera</a> del Gobierno entorpecieron la reacción. Como también la tentación de la derecha opositora, arrastrada por su escisión radical, que le llevó a tontear con la violencia y el enfrentamiento para lograr <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/feijoo-abre-el-curso-politico-con-ceuta-como-arma-de-desgaste-contra-sanchez.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/feijoo-abre-el-curso-politico-con-ceuta-como-arma-de-desgaste-contra-sanchez.html">su sueño húmedo de hacer caer al Gobierno</a> antes de la próxima primavera. Es inteligente que se dieran cuenta de que estaban a punto de provocar una guerra civil entre las dos personalidades que componen la población ceutí y <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-28/el-pp-corrige-su-discurso-y-llama-a-la-calma-y-al-cese-de-la-violencia-en-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-28/el-pp-corrige-su-discurso-y-llama-a-la-calma-y-al-cese-de-la-violencia-en-ceuta.html">llamaron a la calma.</a> Estas carencias se sumaron a un problema de por sí irresoluble, pues la emigración es un caso de libro sobre cómo la desigualdad impide, e impedirá siempre, la convivencia pacífica. Tuvimos que ver incluso a dos ministros de un mismo Gobierno <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-25/marlaska-contradice-a-robles-e-insiste-en-que-el-cni-no-informo-de-la-posibilidad-de-una-entrada-masiva-en-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-25/marlaska-contradice-a-robles-e-insiste-en-que-el-cni-no-informo-de-la-posibilidad-de-una-entrada-masiva-en-ceuta.html">discrepar en público</a> para intentar salvar la cara de sus subordinados. No parece que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/los-servicios-secretos-ven-probables-mas-acciones-encubiertas-sobre-ceuta-y-melilla.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/los-servicios-secretos-ven-probables-mas-acciones-encubiertas-sobre-ceuta-y-melilla.html">los servicios secretos,</a> por más que sea bueno protegerlos, avisaran ni de lejos de la marabunta que sacudió Ceuta los últimos días de julio. Ni tampoco las fuerzas de seguridad fronteriza, por muy avisadas, hubieran tenido el cuajo de disparar balas de goma contra la gente desesperada que a nado trataba de ganar la playa, como había ocurrido anteriormente para indignidad general.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-09-01/ceuta-capital-de-europa.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/MB6XZ2WPKVBQ7MGXQSUMAMLVGU.jpg?auth=ca1829521ebf8f772b5c0fee4d32280b3cf3ec08407a833fb6aa3703c6cd0ab9" width="1309" height="1273" alt="."></img><p>Ha pasado un mes desde que se produjo <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/ceuta-el-mes-que-rompio-una-ciudad.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/ceuta-el-mes-que-rompio-una-ciudad.html">el último cruce masivo de personas</a> a la ciudad autónoma de Ceuta. A lo largo de estas semanas, lo que constituye un incuestionable desafío humanitario y político se ha convertido —por las acciones y omisiones de una respuesta en la que casi nadie sale bien parado— en <a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-30/ceuta-lo-urgente-y-lo-importante.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-08-30/ceuta-lo-urgente-y-lo-importante.html">una grave crisis</a> de consecuencias imprevisibles. La tensión en Ceuta <a href="https://elpais.com/podcasts/hoy-en-el-pais/2026-08-31/ceuta-distintos-miedos-y-una-misma-sensacion-de-abandono-no-podemos-salir-sin-spray-pimienta-y-duermo-escondido-entre-las-canas.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/podcasts/hoy-en-el-pais/2026-08-31/ceuta-distintos-miedos-y-una-misma-sensacion-de-abandono-no-podemos-salir-sin-spray-pimienta-y-duermo-escondido-entre-las-canas.html">se ha hecho insoportable</a> y comienza a derivar en peligrosos abusos y enfrentamientos.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/opinion/2026-09-01/ceuta-la-crisis-que-europa-malinterpreto.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Ceuta: la crisis que Europa malinterpretó

articles.body: <p>La Fiscalía Europea ha recibido una información de Portugal que expone que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-28/la-suspension-de-la-pena-de-aldama-impunidad-o-necesidad-para-investigar-la-corrupcion.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-28/la-suspension-de-la-pena-de-aldama-impunidad-o-necesidad-para-investigar-la-corrupcion.html">Víctor de Aldama</a> y otra serie de empresarios desviaron, presuntamente, entre 2022 y 2024 un total de 27,9 millones de euros procedentes de empresas de hidrocarburos con la finalidad de blanquear ese dinero a través de empresas pantalla radicadas en el país luso. La Fiscalía, encargada de velar por los fondos de la Unión Europea, ha irrumpido así en el <i>caso hidrocarburos </i>que se sigue en la Audiencia Nacional y ha enviado al juez Santiago Pedraz datos de las pesquisas que desplegó Portugal al detectar transferencias sospechosas. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-02/la-fiscalia-europea-irrumpe-en-el-caso-hidrocarburos-y-revela-que-aldama-y-otros-empresarios-desviaron-279-millones-a-portugal.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: La Fiscalía Europea irrumpe en el ‘caso hidrocarburos’ y revela que Aldama y otros empresarios desviaron 27,9 millones a Portugal

articles.body: <p>El Ayuntamiento de Madrid ha acusado este martes al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez de “boicotear” la concentración por Ceuta que el Consistorio ha convocado para este miércoles tras haber recibido un escrito de la Delegación del Gobierno que le reprocha haber solicitado la autorización por la vía del derecho de reunión, pese a que este solo pueden ostentarlo las personas físicas y jurídicas que no sean públicas. Fuentes del Gobierno municipal han informado de que han recibido un escrito de Delegación del Gobierno “en el que comunican al Ayuntamiento de Madrid que prohíben la concentración prevista para mañana en Cibeles”. No obstante, la carta que la Delegación ha enviado a Madrid, consultada por EL PAÍS, dice al final que el Ayuntamiento podrá celebrar la protesta como un acto institucional, como así lo ha confirmado la propia delegación en un comunicado posterior. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/madrid-acusa-al-gobierno-de-boicotear-la-concentracion-por-ceuta-pese-a-que-el-ejecutivo-permitira-que-se-celebre.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Madrid acusa al Gobierno de “boicotear” la concentración por Ceuta pese a que el Ejecutivo permitirá que se celebre

articles.body: <p>Silvia Rojas lleva 22 años destinada en la Fiscalía de Ceuta, por lo que su conocimiento sobre la criminalidad de la ciudad autónoma es exhaustivo. Ella vivió la anterior crisis migratoria de 2021 ya como jefa de área de esa Fiscalía (fue nombrada en octubre de 2020 y <a href="https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2025-22350" target="_self" rel="" title="https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2025-22350">renovada el pasado mes de noviembre de 2025)</a>, pero cree que la situación actual no es ni de lejos comparable. En una entrevista telefónica con EL PAÍS es muy clara: “Me atrevería a decirte que estamos ante un hito sin precedentes en la historia de nuestra nación. Ceuta no puede afrontar por sí sola esta situación. No tiene capacidad”. La fiscal explica que la solución de los menores que todavía siguen en la calle solo puede pasar por que otras comunidades autónomas acojan a niños y niñas, y muestra su preocupación por las agresiones sexuales que, explica, han crecido de forma exponencial desde que el pasado 30 de julio se produjera una entrada masiva. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/la-fiscal-jefa-de-ceuta-hay-casi-una-agresion-sexual-al-dia-hay-preocupacion.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: La fiscal jefa de Ceuta: “Hay casi una agresión sexual al día. Hay preocupación”

"></img><p>El Gobierno hace números y pone nuevo dinero fresco encima de la mesa para demostrar que es falsa la idea del “abandono” de Ceuta del que habla Juan Jesús Vivas, su presidente, una sensación muy extendida en la ciudad. El vicepresidente primero y ministro de Economía, Carlos Cuerpo, desplegó una lluvia de millones en la pantalla de la rueda de prensa del Consejo de Ministros entre ayudas directas a la economía ceutí, gastos en seguridad, atención a inmigrantes y refuerzo de servicios públicos que ascienden a 309 millones de euros. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/el-gobierno-anuncia-un-plan-de-choque-por-valor-de-309-millones-para-ayudar-a-ceuta.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-23/ceuta-la-crisis-imposible.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-23/ceuta-la-crisis-imposible.html">crisis de Ceuta sigue sin tener fin y desborda</a> y monopoliza al Gobierno desde hace un mes en todas sus vertientes, la humanitaria, la social, la política. Después de un mes en silencio, Pedro Sánchez preparó una noticia importante para su primera entrevista de la temporada, su reaparición tras el verano, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html">en la Cadena SER</a>: el Rey visitará Ceuta “en cuanto se den las condiciones”. Precisamente este lunes, según La Moncloa, el Rey y el presidente mantuvieron un encuentro de tres horas en su despacho semanal habitual. Aunque nunca se informa del contenido, es presumible que trataran el asunto que según admitió Sánchez en la entrevista ya han abordado en otras ocasiones. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/sanchez-intenta-bajar-la-presion-prometiendo-una-visita-del-rey-a-ceuta-cuando-se-supere-la-crisis.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/UXAVFH72UFHVJOW3G5PZL5Z74Y.jpg?auth=bd766c4dc458b89898a395e6e8a70e60503ae1a64980eb32391e62db25b650a7" width="3960" height="2640" alt="El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, en el programa 'Hoy por hoy' de la Cadena SER, este lunes. articles.body: <p>Moscú ha conminado al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, a presentar evidencias para <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html">sostener que ha existido —como dijo— una campaña de desinformación rusa</a> en torno a la <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/ceuta-el-mes-que-rompio-una-ciudad.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-30/ceuta-el-mes-que-rompio-una-ciudad.html">crisis de Ceuta</a>. Además, ha recordado que existen canales diplomáticos para formalizar este tipo de acusaciones. “Tenemos una embajada en Madrid. Podrían haber enviado allí las consultas pertinentes. Podrían haber apelado a los mecanismos de Naciones Unidas. Madrid no hizo nada de esto y nadie nos ha dicho nada. En cambio, han corrido tras los micrófonos para hacer declaraciones”, declaró este martes la portavoz del Ministerio de Exteriores ruso, María Zajárova, ante las afirmaciones de Sánchez de que países como Rusia e Israel han contribuido a difundir <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html">bulos para desestabilizar a España</a> tras la irrupción masiva de inmigrantes en Ceuta entre el 30 y 31 de julio.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/rusia-exige-pruebas-a-pedro-sanchez-y-le-acusa-de-correr-tras-los-microfonos.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Rusia se suma a Israel y carga contra Sánchez por vincularlos con los “bulos” sobre Ceuta

articles.body: <p>Era como un fantasma. Hacía cinco años que la Policía Nacional perseguía su sombra, pero nunca le alcanzaba. Cuando los agentes conseguían conocer la identidad falsa bajo la que operaba, el delincuente ya había vuelto a cambiar de nombre. Experto en ciberseguridad, tampoco dejaba pistas digitales y cambiaba su número de teléfono cada dos semanas. “Su capacidad de ocultarse es increíble. Es de los mejores que hemos visto”, cuentan desde el grupo policial que buscaba al narcotraficante más buscado de Alemania desde 2021. Hasta que el pasado 24 de agosto consiguieron <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-06-15/el-crimen-organizado-se-extiende-ya-por-todos-los-rincones-de-la-costa-del-sol.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-06-15/el-crimen-organizado-se-extiende-ya-por-todos-los-rincones-de-la-costa-del-sol.html">dar con él en Málaga durante la visita de su hermano</a>. Ahora se encuentra en prisión a la espera de ser extraditado a Alemania, donde se le buscaba por tráfico de drogas y pertenencia a organización criminal.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/cae-en-malaga-el-narcotraficante-mas-buscado-de-alemania-era-como-un-fantasma.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Cae en Málaga el narcotraficante más buscado de Alemania: “Era como un fantasma”

articles.body: <p>Marruecos no se ha pronunciado oficialmente <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html">ante una eventual visita de Felipe VI a Ceuta</a>, aunque los medios de comunicación se han hecho eco del anuncio efectuado este lunes por el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, en la Cadena SER. Un responsable político y analista de las relaciones bilaterales, que prefiere no ser citado ante la sensibilidad de la cuestión, ha asegurado tras la entrevista del jefe del Ejecutivo que “una visita del rey de España a Ceuta en estos momentos solo serviría para reavivar la crisis”. “Ahora hay que reducir la tensión, intentar encontrar soluciones para el retorno inmediato de las personas que han atravesado la frontera [en la <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-31/miles-de-personas-penetran-durante-la-noche-en-ceuta-en-medio-de-la-pasividad-de-la-policia-marroqui.html#?rel=mas" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-31/miles-de-personas-penetran-durante-la-noche-en-ceuta-en-medio-de-la-pasividad-de-la-policia-marroqui.html#?rel=mas">avalancha migratoria del 30 y el 31 de julio]</a>. Eso es lo importante: encontrar salidas pragmáticas a estos graves problemas, vista la situación que se vive en Ceuta”, ha destacado la fuente política marroquí consultada en Rabat.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/marruecos-observa-como-una-provocacion-una-visita-real-a-ceuta-en-medio-de-su-campana-electoral.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: Marruecos observa como una provocación una visita real a Ceuta en medio de su campaña electoral

articles.body: <p>A finales de verano de 2007, el rey Juan Carlos I expresó “muy encarecidamente” un deseo al entonces presidente José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero en uno de sus despachos habituales: visitar Ceuta y Melilla antes de finalizar su reinado. “Para él era muy importante”, explican fuentes que integraron ese Gobierno socialista y siguieron de cerca lo que supuso la primera y única visita de un jefe del Estado español a las ciudades autónomas tras la Constitución.<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-31/sanchez-destaca-la-cooperacion-instantanea-con-marruecos-y-asegura-que-el-rey-visitara-ceuta.html"> El presidente del Ejecutivo, Pedro Sánchez, aseguró este lunes en una entrevista en la Cadena SER </a>que la foto de un monarca en el territorio, que actualmente sufre una grave crisis migratoria, puede volver a repetirse en breve. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-01/el-dia-que-juan-carlos-i-pidio-encarecidamente-a-zapatero-visitar-ceuta-y-melilla.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: El día que Juan Carlos I pidió “encarecidamente” a Zapatero visitar Ceuta y Melilla

articles.body: <p>La Fiscalía ha mostrado su oposición a <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-15/abalos-pide-al-supremo-que-anule-su-condena-porque-su-caso-debio-juzgarse-en-la-audiencia-nacional.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-07-15/abalos-pide-al-supremo-que-anule-su-condena-porque-su-caso-debio-juzgarse-en-la-audiencia-nacional.html">las quejas que el exministro José Luis Ábalos</a> y su exasesor ministerial Koldo García han presentado contra <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-22/el-supremo-condena-a-abalos-a-24-anos-y-tres-meses-de-carcel-a-koldo-garcia-a-19-anos-y-ocho-meses-y-a-aldama-a-cuatro-anos-y-medio.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-06-22/el-supremo-condena-a-abalos-a-24-anos-y-tres-meses-de-carcel-a-koldo-garcia-a-19-anos-y-ocho-meses-y-a-aldama-a-cuatro-anos-y-medio.html">la sentencia en la que se les condena a 24 años y tres meses de cárcel</a> y 19 años y ocho meses, respectivamente. “Están abocadas al fracaso”, ha asegurado el fiscal jefe de Anticorrupción, Alejandro Luzón. articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) La Generalitat ha decidit eliminar l’accés amb contrasenya a La Meva Salut , l’espai digital personal on cada usuari pot consultar informació sobre el seu historial mèdic, i deixar com a única via d’entrada l’idCAT Mòbil . De moment, les dues formes d’accés conviuran fins al gener del 2027 , és a dir la paraula de pas tradicional o el sistema d’autentificació de dos passos que envia al telèfon d’un usuari prèviament registrat un codi d’accés únic i d’un sol ús. El canvi, però, ja es començarà a nota a partir d’aquest 15 de setembre , quan els usuaris ja no podran generar noves contrasenyes . També et pot interessar Avisen de la bretxa digital en salut: “Cal saber quan donar un QR i quan un full amb lletres grans” Redacció 3 minuts de lectura Salut vol reforçar la seguretat de les dades mèdiques El Departament de Salut va activar el sistema de doble autenticació el gener del 2025 per reforçar la seguretat a l’hora d’accedir a La Meva Salut. Des d’aleshores, quan s’entra a l’espai amb l’opció de contrasenya, es rep un codi numèric únic per SMS al telèfon registrat al sistema, que s’ha d’introduir en una nova pantalla per completar l’autenticació i accedir al servei. La mesura s’aplica tant a la versió web com a l’aplicació mòbil i s’emmarcava en un conjunt d’accions per reforçar la seguretat després que el 2024 es detectessin robatoris de credencials personals per accedir-hi. En aquest mateix context es va incorporar l’idCAT Mòbil com a sistema alternatiu d’identificació, es va reforçar la seguretat de les contrasenyes personals i es va introduir la notificació automàtica per correu electrònic cada vegada que es modifiquen les dades de contacte associades a La Meva Salut (correu electrònic o número de telèfon) per garantir-ne una protecció addicional. També et pot interessar Nova eina per integrar les imatges mèdiques fetes en centres privats a La Meva Salut Laura Siles 1 minut de lectura Crítiques de familiars de persones grans L’anunci de retirar l’accés amb contrasenya a La Meva Salut ha generat nombroses crítiques d’usuaris i familiars de persones grans . Consideren que el canvi agreuja la bretxa digital i suposa una complicació més per a la gestió familiar d’aquesta aplicació. Per exemple, el cas de molts fills que gestionen La Meva Salut dels seus pares a través del seu mòbil, on guardaven l’usuari i la contrasenya, i rebien l’SMS de confirmació. Ara en canvi, amb el nou sistema, el mateix telèfon no es pot vincular a dues identitats digitals diferents. @salutcat com haig de fer l'accés de "La meva salut" de la meva mare? Ella no té smartphone. Desgraciadament totes dues utilitzem molt aquest servei i no tinc cap més opció que utilizar el meu número de mòbil per a totes dues. — Voland (@Voland_66) August 31, 2026 Els fills acabarem tenint dos números de telèfons per fer les gestions dels pares. Quin pare de més de 70 sap utilitzar la Meva Salut????? És un sense sentit de merda de gestió. I no diguem que funciona com el cul i ni els metges saben fer la servir — Reclamacions Mediques (@RMediques) August 30, 2026 Arran de les queixes, la síndica de greuges de Catalunya , Esther Giménez-Salinas, ha reclamat al Departament de Salut que ampliï les opcions de representació de La Meva Salut. La síndica considera que cal garantir la protecció de les dades sense impedir l’acompanyament digital i assegura que el Departament de Salut està estudiant alternatives que es podrien aplicar de cara al 2027. articles.body: El Futbol Club Barcelona ha fet oficial la cessió de Marc Casadó al Deportivo de la Corunya després que ambdós clubs hagin arribat a un acord en les últimes hores de mercat. Tot i que Casadó en un principi no volia marxar del club , finalment l’operació s’ha tancat i el club gallec tindrà una opció de compra de 30 milions d’euros a finals de temporada. El Barça haurà d’assumir bona part de la fitxa durant la temporada. També et pot interessar Les perles de la Masia que han robat el cor de Hansi Flick durant la pretemporada del Barça Àlex Masana 2 minuts de lectura Nova etapa per a un dels jugadors amb més sentiment blaugrana El Deportivo de la Corunya és el destí d’un dels jugadors del vestidor amb més sentiment blaugrana . Culer de tota la vida, ho ha demostrat moltes vegades celebrant les victòries culers a Canaletes , quan no era jugador del primer equip i, fins i tot, quan ha format part del primer equip blaugrana. Va arribar al Barça amb 13 anys , procedent del CF Damm, però abans havia jugat al CF Vilamajor, PB Sant Celoni i al Granollers. A la base blaugrana va passar pel cadet A, pel juvenil B i el juvenil A, en aquest últim es va proclamar campió de Lliga i va aconseguir la Copa de Campions la temporada 2020-21, lluint el braçalet de capità. També et pot interessar Ronald Araujo: acord de cessió entre el Barça i el Liverpool Gemma Garriga 2 minuts de lectura Rafa Márquez i Hansi Flick, entrenadors clau per a Casadó La temporada 22-23 va fer el salt al Barça Atlètic sota les ordres de Rafa Márquez i es va convertir en un dels jugadors importants del mexicà . Casadó va disputar 36 partits i va disputar la semifinal d’ascens a la Segona Divisió, en la qual van caure amb el Reial Madrid Castilla. Temporada en què va fer també el seu debut amb el primer equip, a la Lliga de Campions , va ser l’1 de novembre del 2022, al camp del Viktoria Pilsen amb victòria blaugrana per 2 a 4. L’arribada de Hansi Flick l’estiu del 2024 va ser clau per al migcampista blaugrana , la confiança de l’entrenador alemany li va permetre disputar fins a 36 partits entre totes les competicions, 29 d’ells de titular, amb un total de 2.449 minuts disputats i va aconseguir la Lliga, la Copa del Rei i la Supercopa d’Espanya. Aquest últim curs la seva presència a l’equip no ha estat la mateixa , tot i jugar 34 partits en total, només en 15 va ser titular i els minuts van disminuir a 1.395. Va tornar a guanyar la Lliga i la Supercopa d’Espanya. També et pot interessar Marc Casadó, la seva suplència i el rol titular de Frenkie de Jong en una entrevista a betevé 1 minut de lectura

articles.body: En les darreres hores del mercat d’estiu, Monchi ha fet un canvi de cromos a l’Espanyol . Rubén Sánchez marxa a l’Elx i al lateral dret hi arriba Andoni Gorosabel , cedit de l’Athletic Club. La operació contempla una opció de compra. Els blanc-i-blaus tanquen d’aquesta manera el setè i últim fitxatge per afrontar el curs 2026/2027 . Un lateral solvent i amb potencial ofensiu Gorosabel, de 30 anys, aterra procedent de l’ Athletic Club —amb qui ha guanyat una Copa del Rei — i també ha jugat a la Reial Societat i a l’Alabès . Suma gairebé 200 partits al màxim nivell i havent disputat competició europea. És un lateral solvent, d’intensitat defensiva notable i amb bon criteri per incorporar-se a l’atac. A l’Athletic , aquest curs Edin Terzic no comptava amb ell ja que es decantava per Jesús Areso i Hugo Rincón al carril dret. Ara enceta una nova etapa il·lusionant a l’Espanyol.
